beta_new: A tough, low roof opens the route; beyond it you pump through steeply overhanging stone full of pockets, and a boulder problem guards the chain anchors at the finish.

From a small pedestal, drift up and to the left via thin runnels, sidepulls, deep horizontal breaks and plates, picking your way over the featured slab to a roomy ledge. Slip off your shoes at the anchors and enjoy the view.
Begin beside a big jumble of boulders and climb the bolted face via little sharp pockets and edges, finishing up a flake that faces right to the chains.
Step off the boulder pile and stay with the bolted arete throughout, ending at the anchors.

Begin with pitch one of The Corner, which delivers you under the roof. Stretch way out beyond the lip for a good hold and a perfect 1.5 tricam slot in an upright crack, then pull over and finish on the face higher up, which is rated 5.10.
Ascend the thin face beside a neighbouring dihedral, on its left, until you meet a roof's left end at which a crack starts, put in gear at that spot, then complete the climb on another route.
Begin by following the route before it to the shelf twenty-five feet off the ground, then take the pleasant hand-width split in the face to your right to another ledge.

moves.from: Rappel there, or link into the last pitch of Groundhog to top out.

beta_new: It shares a face with its neighbour South of Zimbabwe, though past the bolt it angles upward and rightward to horizontal breaks. Get gear in, follow a flake, then pull hard to the top.

Start with the clean first dihedral of the neighbouring route, then traverse leftward along a shelf under the roof on the left. Place gear, then follow the faint corner and rounded edge to the anchors. Pitch two crosses the wall to the big ledge.
Clamber up onto boulders to start, then pass iron-hard jugs and a low empty bolt hole before slanting leftward to the chain anchors beneath a high roof.
Gain the ledge via four bolts on the green wall below, take a breather there, then launch onto the bolted arete, which ends at an anchor close to the rim.

Share the opening of Injured: step onto a low boulder shaped like a ledge and find two bolts side by side. Go directly to the left one, then clip the right one, and slant upward to the right across gray, platy stone to the quick-link anchors.

Begin left of a chest-high flake that faces left. Pass a large hueco ledge on its left side onto a platform atop a small pillar, then tackle very steep rock beside a short, overhanging dihedral, aiming for a horizontal shelf. A greenish section follows, then an orange featured stretch leads to the chain anchor.
Stay on the face beside the obtuse dihedral rather than in the dihedral itself, and protect with natural gear.
Start in the right-hand crack of the pair, then switch left partway and fight a pump onto the ledge.

Start from the boulder fronting the route, step across and enter the split, hanging tight for roughly fifteen feet. Higher, a pod and assorted odd features lead to the ledge at the top; you belay using the anchors of the neighbouring route.

Follow the left-hand crack of the pair to a ledge about twenty-five feet up, then carry on along the slim corner under a last roof. Either chimney the slot or exit rightward on face holds. Descend by rappelling off the ledge, or add the brief second pitch to reach the summit.
Start on the slab beside a neighbouring bolted line, clip three bolts, then switch to small and medium cams for the stretch leading to the ledge.

moves.from: switch to small and medium cams for the stretch leading to the ledge

beta_new: Take the right-hand crack until it dies out, then work along the thin wall onto a ledge. Easier face climbing leads from there to the bolted anchors.
Climb to a horizontal break and place gear, then stretch out, let go and crank past the lip of the eight-foot roof into a slot of offwidth size. A finger crack leads from there to the fixed anchors.
Climb the offwidth to the perch.

moves.from: then either rappel off the tree or move across leftward to continue on the neighbouring route's second pitch

beta_new: A steep start gets you onto a ledge for the hands, the face above is more vertical, and the overhanging headwall at the top is the final test before the chains.
Begin a few feet over from the previous route and pull on pockets for four bolts to reach a vertical section. Pass it, then deal with the increasingly steep rock above.
Two bolts of steep rock bring you to a big ledge; a chunky flake leads to a second ledge, and steeper rock above takes you to the anchors.

Start via the crack when it is dry, otherwise the face on its left. Abandon the large holds and step right to clip bolt two, find a rest above, then bust up the brief, pumpy headwall on single-pad edges.
Begin on a boulder and step into a traverse that angles up and right, then go directly upward through the fingery wall, make the final clip and blast the last stretch to the chains.

A handful of big moves start things, then it is a race through connected pockets and little crimps. Nothing gives a rest, and a short roof comes right before the chains, so a fall there means starting over.
Follow the hand crack up to a shelf with a big boulder and a tree, then keep going up the wide section to the anchors of the neighbouring route.
Most parties stop after pitch one since higher sections are dirty. Layback the flake, step around the roof's left end, and clip a few more bolts to the chains.
Follow a swept strip across a sharply angled slab, and a bulge, up to the anchors beneath the big roof, with pitch two then continuing past it.
Steep, rewarding movement on good holds follows a broken pale streak. A bolted slab leads first to a roof, after which the rock becomes blockier and steeper along a dike.
Pitch one heads up and left over a small roof, then continues over solid stone to a bolt and on to an easier slab. Pitch two climbs a corner, then moves rightward across a face to a tree.

Start with the bottom slab to the bolted belay, then angle up and left across simple rock toward a brief dihedral. Stem it, surmount a bulge using a finger crack, and finish via steep fractured cracks.
Edge your way left up the black slab, passing four bolts, then escape left beneath the roof via a crack you can hand-traverse to the anchor.
A delicate face climb past six bolts on a steep slab, finishing in the awkward, moss-covered dihedral near the top.
Smear along the black streak's right side past five bolts to the corner that angles left, pull over a roof on the right, then use a crack angling right to reach the steep headwall.
Use delicate face moves, clipping three bolts.

Pitch one follows intermittent cracks and corners beside a thin white stripe. Pitch two edges up that steep, featureless-looking wall, protected by Tricams plus Friends placed in pockets, and eases toward the top.

moves.from: protected by Tricams plus Friends placed in pockets

beta_new: Haul on jugs through a succession of small overhangs with good gear throughout; scramble the small ledges toward the first overhang, then keep following solid holds across four overhangs up to a belay on a large boulder.
Start facing the big tree used as a belay anchor, go directly to the overhang, then power and smear beyond the roof, just rightward of a minuscule corner.
